item.title: Why iPhones are so expensive in India again
item.description: Apple's new iPhones cost more this year, not just the Duo, its first foldable, or the 18 Pro. Older models went up too, breaking a five-year run of steady pricing in India. Some of that is tax and currency. Most of it is a global memory shortage, squeezed by AI's appetite for chips. Add India's duty structure and Apple's read on what buyers will pay, and the entry fee for an iPhone has never been higher.

item.title: 1980s AI Photo trend: 5 ChatGPT prompts to create Kerala-style retro images
item.description: A social media trend uses ChatGPT to recreate photos in 1980s styles. Users are now focusing on regional aesthetics, specifically 1980s Kerala and Malayali culture. Prompts request authentic family, wedding, college, and studio portraits from the period. These images incorporate traditional clothing, jewellery, and home settings from Kerala. The AI maintains recognizable facial features while adding retro photographic elements.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Deadly plot by ‘killer bahu’: Kanpur bizman sensed danger, but ended up with 26 stab wounds
item.description: An alleged murder plot to stage a heart attack was foiled when the victim returned home. The intended suffocation plan changed to a violent stabbing after the victim discovered the attackers. The victim sustained 26 stab wounds during the assault which occurred late at night. The alleged conspirator was reportedly dancing at a lounge while the killing unfolded.
item.dc:creator: PRACHI KUMAWAT

item.title: Lavrov arrives in India ahead of Brics Summit; Putin to arrive shortly
item.description: The 18th BRICS Summit is set to take place in New Delhi on September 12-13, bringing together world leaders, including Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping. With a focus on pivotal discussions surrounding economic cooperation, technology, energy, and global governance, the summit will address pressing issues such as food and energy security, alongside current global trade tensions. This gathering aims to strengthen resilience, innovation, and sustainable collaboration among member nations.

item.title: 22-year-old pleads guilty in US' biggest Bitcoin theft; spent millions on cars & more
item.description: A 22-year-old organized a scheme stealing over 4,100 Bitcoin from an investor. The stolen cryptocurrency was then spent on luxury items and lavish experiences. Investigators traced the digital trail through a missed IP address, leading to arrests. Several defendants have pleaded guilty, and others are awaiting sentencing in the ongoing case. This incident highlights the growing threat of social engineering in cryptocurrency fraud.

item.description: Gwyneth Paltrow bought about 2.4 acres in Montecito for $4.9 million in 2016, razed the existing structures and embarked on a ground-up project that took about six years. The result was a roughly 14,000-square-foot home powered by solar energy and equipped with a graywater system.

item.description: Apple has launched its first foldable iPhone Duo and iPhone 18 Pro models. item.title: Tiger Woods and Vanessa Trump’s wealth: How did they build their fortunes?
item.description: Vanessa Trump's wealth stems from family investments and real estate holdings. Tiger Woods built a diverse business empire through golf and various ventures. Woods' TGR Ventures oversees golf course design and sports entertainment projects. His portfolio includes fashion, hospitality, and technology investments. Both individuals have significant real estate assets contributing to their financial standing.

item.title: Caitlin Clark’s $4.5bn brand empire: How is she expanding her influence?
item.description: Caitlin Clark has expanded her growing off-court profile with a new collection from a major drinkware brand valued at an estimated $4.5 billion. The partnership builds on their collaboration that began in 2025, featuring tumblers and bottles in Clark’s Future design. The Indiana Fever star already boasts major deals with Nike, Gatorade, State Farm and Wilson, highlighting how her influence continues to extend beyond basketball.

item.title: Congress-NC rift over Vande Mataram: The ghost of 1987 and ‘big brother’ complex
item.description: The alliance between the NC and Congress is witnessing persistent tensions regarding political leadership. Recent arguments over the Vande Mataram reveal significant ideological rifts. Echoes of past events, such as the contentious 1987 election, continue to influence NC's political behavior. The long-term success of this coalition hinges on its ability to balance conflicting priorities as they tackle statehood and Article 370 challenges.

item.title: US govt proposes scrapping 60-day grace period for foreign workers after job loss
item.description: The US Department of Homeland Security is considering the elimination of a 60-day grace period for specific visa holders, which could greatly affect Indian H-1B and L-1 visa holders in the United States. This proposal is based on the belief that the grace period compromises the integrity of employment-related visa classifications. A decision to remove this grace period would introduce significant financial and logistical hurdles for those impacted.

item.title: Shafali stars with 64, Deepti strikes thrice as India storm into 10th Asia Cup final
item.description: India secured a dominant 40-run victory over Bangladesh to advance into the Women's Asia Cup 2026 final. Shafali Varma's explosive 64-run innings provided a strong foundation for India's competitive total. India's bowlers applied sustained pressure, restricting Bangladesh to 109 runs in their chase. Deepti Sharma was instrumental with the ball, claiming crucial wickets throughout the match. This win extends India's unbeaten streak and sends them to their tenth consecutive final.

item.title: Akash stares at BSP exit: Why Mayawati decided to 'free' nephew ahead of UP polls
item.description: Amid political turmoil, Akash Anand has again been demoted by Mayawati, who has questioned her nephew's maturity. His X profile has devolved from National Convenor to Party Worker and now to Supporter. His younger sibling, Ishan Anand, has been brought to the centre stage. Mayawati freed Akash political prospects to his father-in-law's exit from the scene, as the BSP confronts a challenging landscape with dwindling votes and approaching UP elections.

item.title: Shree Charani creates history at 22, becomes fastest Indian to 50 T20I wickets
item.description: Shree Charani has made history by becoming the fastest Indian bowler to take fifty wickets in women's T20 internationals, completing this achievement in her twenty-ninth T20I appearance. This pivotal moment elevates her status among the world's top bowlers. Furthermore, India's journey in the Asia Cup semifinal has added to the excitement surrounding her performance in international cricket.

item.title: ‘Are you in relationship?’ How woman 'manipulated' ex-staffer to kill father-in-law
item.description: Investigators found WhatsApp messages indicating Shalu urged Vishal Gautam to murder her father-in-law. Shalu and Vishal engaged in conversations for months, with Shalu complimenting Vishal and inquiring about his relationship status. Police believe Shalu manipulated Vishal into planning and executing the murder of Vineet Minocha. Vishal erased chat history but failed to remove all WhatsApp call records, which investigators recovered.

item.title: Root scripts history, surpasses Smith to become the fielder with most catches in Tests
item.description: On Thursday, Joe Root made history in Test cricket by claiming his 220th catch, overtaking Steve Smith's record. This monumental achievement took place during England's third Test against Pakistan, where they built a commanding lead in the first innings. Meanwhile, Pakistan struggled early in their second innings, facing significant challenges at the crease.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: Missile with ‘eyes’: Iran’s new missile can hunt targets without GPS, putting US warships on alert
item.description: Recent reports indicate that Iran deployed electro-optical guided missiles against US warships, showcasing a technology that enables precise target identification without GPS reliance. The US Central Command has acknowledged these attacks, affirming that all efforts were unsuccessful. This escalation follows US responses to Iranian oil tanker actions, intensifying tensions in the Strait of Hormuz area.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Algeria cuts diplomatic ties with UAE over 'provocative, hostile' actions
item.description: In a notable diplomatic shift, Algeria has officially severed ties with the United Arab Emirates, following a period of escalating tensions. The nations disagree on key regional matters, particularly concerning Western Sahara and the Sahel, with Algeria accusing the UAE of hostile provocations. This rift also underscores contrasting positions on Israel and Middle Eastern relations, marking a crucial break in bilateral relations between the two countries.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: US built taller smokestacks to cut local pollution; acid rain spread farther
item.description: In an effort to mitigate local air pollution, American power companies constructed towering smokestacks, effectively releasing sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides into higher winds. Unfortunately, this practice contributed to acid rain, harming ecosystems throughout North America. In response, Congress revised the Clean Air Act to restrict the use of tall stacks and improve emission control by emphasizing source capture instead.
